the deformation of fine-grained quartz aggregates at high temperature and low pressure (i.e., 600 to 750 °C and 1 to 1.2 GPa) is controlled by diffusion creep, whereas at high temperature and high pressure (i.e. 800 to 950 ° C and 1.3 to 1.6 GPa) deformation is controlled by a combination of grain boundary and dislocation creep.

the deformation and rheology of quartz aggregates with fine grain sizes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deformation mechanism in fine-grained quartz aggregates at high temperatures and low strain rates is a combination of intragranular and grain-boundary processes.
the flow law for quartz is dependent on grain size and temperature and that the flow law at high temperatures is a mixed dislocation and diffusion creep law.
the deformation of quartz is a complex process that involves dislocation creep as well as grain boundary diffusion and/or dislocation diffusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deformation behavior of fine-grained quartz is controlled by a combination of grain boundary and dislocation creep processes, where the grain boundary processes dominate at higher temperatures.

The main takeaway from our work is that
fine‐grained quartz deforms by a mixed mechanism of dislocation and diffusion creep, and the relative contribution of each mechanism depends on temperature, water fugacity, and grain size.
